newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to pursue Palestinian aid despite wastage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to pursue Palestinian aid despite wastage.

text.p: The United States will pursue its aid programme to the Palestinians despite alleged squandering of funds by Palestinian ministers and a furore over land sales to Jews, the State Department said on Tuesday.

"We will continue the American aid programme with the Palestinians because we think it's beneficial to the people of the West Bank and Gaza Strip. It supports the peace negotiations," spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
Donor nations who have pledged $3.4 billion to the Palestinians since the PLO signed a 1993 peace deal with Israel hold an annual meeting in Washington Thursday to review the flow of aid.
But a report issued last month by Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat's auditing office, which charged that some ministers squandered $326 million last year, has prompted concern among donors.
Anis al-Qaq, deputy minister of planning and international cooperation, said Tuesday that no donor funds were involved, and Burns said no U.S. aid had gone astray.
"We can account for every dollar and every cent of what the American taxpayer has sent to the West Bank and Gaza Strip," Burns told a news briefing.

He said the U.S. aid programme, totalling $500 million over five years, was supported by the Israeli government and went straight into aid projects rather than being paid to the self-rule Palestinian Authority.
"We will be sending the Palestinian people a very negative signal indeed if we pull the rug out from under the assistance programme," he said.

The chairmen of two key Congressional committees threatened last month to block further U.S. aid to the Palestinians unless they withdrew a law barring sale of private land to Jews. The recent killing of three Arabs allegedly involved in such sales has caused uproar in Israel.

The threat came in a letter to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright from Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jesse Helms and House International Relations Committee chairman Benjamin Gilman. Albright has yet to reply.
Burns reaffirmed strong U.S. condemnation of any incitement by Palestinian officials to violence against people who sold land to Jews.
He said the Palestinians "must make unequivocally clear statements against political assassinations", but did not answer directly when asked if the United States would tie its aid to the land issue.
